description: BUG 1: No translations appear because OCR reads FIXED screen regions (hardcoded for 1920x1080) but GW2 tooltips render WHERE THE MOUSE IS. Make OCR follow the mouse cursor by default: each capture cycle, compute a region (~500x400 default) centered near the current cursor position, converted to client/backbuffer coordinates, and OCR that region. Keep fixed regions from config as a fallback (used when follow-mouse is disabled). Add diagnostic logging of the OCR-recognized text and whether a dictionary translation was found. This feature is independent of FEAT-002 and FEAT-003 but touches the same overlay module for the HWND accessor, so it should land before or coordinate with FEAT-002.
steps: Add config fields in src/config/config.h: bool m_ocrFollowMouse = true; int m_ocrFollowWidth = 500; int m_ocrFollowHeight = 400; with matching const getters ocrFollowMouse(), ocrFollowWidth(), ocrFollowHeight() (thread-safe via shared_lock, following the existing getter pattern).

In src/config/config.cpp: parse the new fields in loadInternal() (json.contains checks with .get<bool>()/.get<int>(), same style as existing fields: keys 'ocr_follow_mouse', 'ocr_follow_width', 'ocr_follow_height'), and serialize them in save() alongside the other json[...] assignments.

In config/bronco_config.json: add "ocr_follow_mouse": true, "ocr_follow_width": 500, "ocr_follow_height": 400 near the OCR settings. Keep the existing ocr_regions array intact (it is the fallback when follow-mouse is disabled).

Expose the game window handle for coordinate conversion: in src/overlay/imgui_overlay.h declare 'HWND gameWindow();' and in src/overlay/imgui_overlay.cpp implement it to return the stored g_hwnd (the value passed to overlay::initialize, which is desc.OutputWindow from present_hook.cpp). Document with a /// comment.

In src/pipeline/pipeline.cpp workerThread(): before building the region arrays, check bronco::Config::instance().ocrFollowMouse(). When true, compute a single follow-mouse region: call GetCursorPos(&pt) to get screen coords, then if a valid HWND is available (bronco::overlay::gameWindow()) call ScreenToClient(hwnd, &pt) to convert to client coordinates that match the captured backbuffer pixel space. Build a ScreenRegion centered on the cursor: x = cursorClientX - width/2, y = cursorClientY - height/2, width = Config::ocrFollowWidth(), height = Config::ocrFollowHeight(). Clamp x,y,width,height so the region lies fully within [0,width)x[0,height) of the captured frame (recognizeRegions in ocr_engine.cpp SKIPS any region that is out of bounds, so clamping is required or the follow region will be silently dropped). Use this single region instead of Config::ocrRegions() for that cycle. When ocrFollowMouse() is false, keep the existing Config::ocrRegions() path unchanged.

Add diagnostic logging in src/pipeline/pipeline.cpp after g_ocrLoader.processFrame returns and while building overlayEntries: for each BroncoOcrResult log the recognized original text and whether a translation was found (heuristic: translated is non-empty AND differs from original -> 'translation found', else 'no dictionary match'). Build a std::string message and pass .c_str() to bronco::log::info(...), matching the existing logging style. Also log the computed follow-mouse region coordinates once per capture at info level so region placement can be diagnosed. Guard against log spam if practical (e.g., only log when text is non-empty).

Update README.md (Configuracao table and Regioes OCR section) and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md to document the new follow-mouse mode as the default and the three new config keys (ocr_follow_mouse, ocr_follow_width, ocr_follow_height), noting that fixed ocr_regions are used as a fallback when ocr_follow_mouse is false. Use ASCII-only text consistent with the existing docs (no accented characters, matching the file's current style).
acceptance_criteria: config/bronco_config.json contains ocr_follow_mouse (true), ocr_follow_width (500), ocr_follow_height (400) and still contains the ocr_regions array.
Config exposes ocrFollowMouse()/ocrFollowWidth()/ocrFollowHeight() getters, parses the keys in loadInternal(), and serializes them in save().

Pipeline::workerThread computes a cursor-centered region via GetCursorPos + ScreenToClient when follow-mouse is enabled, clamps it to the captured frame bounds, and falls back to Config::ocrRegions() when disabled.
bronco::overlay::gameWindow() is declared in the header and returns the stored g_hwnd.
Pipeline logs the OCR-recognized text and whether a dictionary translation was found, plus the computed follow region coordinates, via bronco::log::info.
README.md and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md document the follow-mouse default and the new config keys.
Header and implementation signatures stay in sync; the region-clamping logic guarantees the region passed to OCR satisfies x>=0, y>=0, x+width<=frameWidth, y+height<=frameHeight.
verification: Static review: confirm the clamped region always satisfies recognizeRegions() bounds checks in src/ocr/ocr_engine.cpp (x>=0 && y>=0 && x+width<=screenWidth && y+height<=screenHeight) so it is never silently skipped.
Static review: confirm ScreenToClient is called with the game HWND and that a null/zero HWND is handled gracefully (fall back to raw cursor coords or skip conversion).
Static review: confirm config.h getter declarations, config.cpp definitions, loadInternal parsing, and save() serialization all reference the same three keys.

Cannot compile on Linux; do not run cmake. Confirm no obvious C++ syntax errors and that includes (Windows.h for GetCursorPos/ScreenToClient) are present in pipeline.cpp (it already includes pipeline.h which includes Windows.h).
findings:
Implemented BUG1 (OCR follows mouse cursor by default). Changes: (1) src/config/config.h: added members m_ocrFollowMouse=true, m_ocrFollowWidth=500, m_ocrFollowHeight=400 and const getters ocrFollowMouse()/ocrFollowWidth()/ocrFollowHeight() following the existing shared_lock getter pattern. (2) src/config/config.cpp: parse keys ocr_follow_mouse/ocr_follow_width/ocr_follow_height in loadInternal() and serialize them in save(); added the three getter definitions. (3) config/bronco_config.json: added the three keys near OCR settings; kept ocr_regions array intact as fallback. (4) src/overlay/imgui_overlay.h + .cpp: declared and implemented HWND gameWindow() returning stored g_hwnd (documented with ///). (5) src/pipeline/pipeline.cpp workerThread(): when Config::ocrFollowMouse() is true, computes ONE region via GetCursorPos + ScreenToClient(gameWindow()) centered on the cursor (width/height from config), clamps region size to the frame and clamps x/y so x>=0,y>=0,x+w<=frameW,y+h<=frameH (guarantees recognizeRegions() bounds check passes and region is never silently skipped). Null/zero HWND handled gracefully (falls back to raw screen cursor coords). When follow-mouse is disabled or GetCursorPos fails, falls back to Config::ocrRegions() unchanged. Added includes <algorithm>, <string>, and ocr_engine.h. (6) Diagnostic logging via bronco::log::info: logs the computed follow region coords once per capture, and for each OCR result logs the recognized original text and whether a dictionary translation was found (heuristic: translated non-empty AND != original => found, else no match); skips empty text to reduce spam. (7) README.md (Configuracao table + Regioes OCR section) and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md updated to document the follow-mouse default and the 3 new keys, ASCII-only. Verification: static review only (Linux sandbox, no MSVC/Windows SDK/DirectX/vcpkg per context.json; did not run cmake). Confirmed header/impl signatures in sync, config parse/save/getters reference the same 3 keys, ScreenToClient uses the game HWND with null-HWND fallback, and the clamp math satisfies recognizeRegions() bounds. GetCursorPos/ScreenToClient are available via Windows.h included by pipeline.h. Did not commit or push (per delegation instructions).

REMEDIATION PASS (addressing review 2026-08-27-020000-review.md, NEEDS_CHANGES): Reworked the follow-mouse region computation in src/pipeline/pipeline.cpp workerThread() to fix the two blocking/should-fix concerns. (BLOCKING #1 client-vs-backbuffer coordinate space) After ScreenToClient yields window-client coordinates, the cursor point is now scaled into the captured backbuffer pixel space using the window's client rect from GetClientRect(hwnd, &clientRect): clientW=right-left, clientH=bottom-top; when clientW != frameWidth the x is scaled by (frameWidth/clientW) and when clientH != frameHeight the y is scaled by (frameHeight/clientH). Scaling uses double-precision intermediate math to avoid int overflow/truncation, then the region is clamped exactly as before (x>=0, y>=0, x+w<=width, y+h<=height) so recognizeRegions() bounds check still passes and the region is never silently skipped. Division-by-zero is impossible: the scale is inside a guard requiring clientW>0 && clientH>0, and the divisors are clientW/clientH. When client size == backbuffer size the scale is a no-op (unchanged behavior for native fullscreen). Added a comment explaining the client->backbuffer scaling. (SHOULD-FIX #2 null/zero HWND fallback) The follow region is now only built when GetCursorPos succeeds AND gameWindow() returns a non-null HWND AND GetClientRect succeeds AND the client rect is non-zero (clientW>0 && clientH>0). In any of those failure cases we no longer build a region from raw unconverted screen coordinates; instead we push nothing, so the existing 'regions.empty() -> Config::ocrRegions()' path falls back to the fixed regions. ScreenToClient/scaling are applied only inside that valid-HWND, valid-client-rect branch. (INFORMATIONAL #3 translation-found heuristic) Left as-is: translated != original is an acceptable diagnostic signal; a true identity translation will log 'no dictionary match', a known false negative that does not affect runtime behavior, only the diagnostic log wording. (INFORMATIONAL #4 ALT-press arm latency) In FEAT-002, not touched; it is a fail-safe <=1-frame latency, not a bug. Also enriched the per-cycle follow-region log to include the client rect size, frame size, and scaled cursor position for diagnosis. Verification: static review only (Linux sandbox, no MSVC/Windows SDK per context.json; did not run cmake). Confirmed: GetClientRect/RECT available via Windows.h (pipeline.h includes it); scaling guarded against divide-by-zero; clamp still satisfies recognizeRegions() bounds (x>=0,y>=0,x+w<=frameW,y+h<=frameH); gameWindow() accessor present in imgui_overlay.h; bronco::log::info(const char*) signature matches. Header/impl remain in sync (no signature changes in this pass).
